subject: Proposal: Hybrid Reserved Pool + GPU Indexation for NimbusAI
messages:
From: Tom Haynes <tom@NimbusAI.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: gpu-ops@nimbusai.com
Date: 2027-03-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sizing ask: committed pool + spot overlay

Hi Aisha,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the throughput looked great. We need a proposal that ties committed capacity to a flexible pricing mechanism. High level: Nimbus wants a 12–24 month reserved pool (we're leaning 18 months) but with a route to swap SKUs between A100/RTX variants and an indexation clause so list-price GPU swings don't force us into an immediate re-negotiation.

Key asks:
- Initial committed vGPU equivalent: 1.2M token-hours / month peak (we can provide trace-based profile tomorrow).
- SKU flexibility: ability to exchange up to 20% of committed capacity across certified GPU families once per quarter.
- Price indexation: tie per-GPU unit price to a 3-month rolling GPU spot index with a +/-10% collar and an annual true-up.
- Early exit: limited credits for rebalancing if cloud GPU supply forces us to downscale.

Can Redwood put together a version that includes an explicit cost sensitivity appendix (showing effect of +/- 25% GPU list price change) and recommended approval path for discounts >20%? We're also happy to have Beth from GPUPartner looped in on the indexation math.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — we're targeting procurement sign-off by end of month for a start in May.

Best,
Tom
Head of Platform
NimbusAI

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Tom Haynes <tom@NimbusAI.com>
Date: 2027-03-07T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing ask: committed pool + spot overlay

Tom —

Thanks, I got this. We'll draft a proposal that includes: committed pool sizing options (12/18/24 mo), SKU exchange mechanics, and a GPU-price index appendix with a sample sensitivity table. I copied Markus (pricing) and Laura (finance/commercial) to outline approvals; Priyom from product will weigh in on technical constraints for SKU swaps.

Two quick Qs so we size correctly:
1) Is the 1.2M token-hour peak a hard ceiling or a monthly average target that spikes?
2) Any regulatory constraints (EU data residency, additional logging) we should include in the Dedicated plan?

I'll push a draft by EOD Wednesday and include a conservative vs aggressive sizing scenario.

— Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-08T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Nimbus sizing + indexation — pricing sensitivity and approval recommendation

Aisha / Laura —

Forwarding Tom's note. Initial thoughts on sensitivity/approvals: we can model a base list price and then two discount buckets: standard commercial (up to 15% off list via reserved commitment) and strategic discount (>15% requires VP approval and finance sign-off). If they want an indexation clause we should:

- Limit the adjustment frequency to quarterly with a symmetric collar of +/-10% relative to our base list for the committed SKU mix.
- Use a third-party GPU spot index (Beth suggested GPUPartner) as the reference.
- Include a floor: minimum effective price no lower than 75% of current list if demand spikes downward (protect Redwood).

Attachments: I sketched a sensitivity table (gpu-price-index-template.xlsx) showing scenarios: base, -25%, +25% and the resulting effective revenue. For any scenario where the effective discount exceeds 22% we need a documented escalation to VP Sales + Finance.

Laura — can you confirm the approval path and whether we can pre-authorize a margin-preservation clause (e.g., dynamic minimum price) to avoid frequent renegotiations?

-Markus
Head of Pricing | Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-09T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Nimbus sizing + indexation — pricing sensitivity and approval recommendation

Markus / Aisha —

Quick confirmation from finance: we can support an indexation clause with the following constraints:
1) Any effective revenue impact > 18% against our forecast requires EVP Finance sign-off.
2) A minimum effective price floor (75% of list) is acceptable; we prefer a dynamic floor tied to committed utilization thresholds (i.e., floor applies only if utilization >= 60%).
3) SKU exchange: allow the 20% per-quarter swap but require SKU parity (same vGPU-equivalent throughput) and a one-time rebalancing fee to cover provisioning.

Recommend we offer an 18-month base term with optional 6-month extension, and include a clear waterfall showing how discounts change with longer tenors and higher committed volume. I can greenlight up to 15% pricing concession in commercial terms; anything beyond that goes to VP Sales.

I'll review the sensitivity file and push comments inline. Marking this as "finance provisionally approved" pending finalized math.

Laura Bennett
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Tom Haynes <tom@NimbusAI.com>
Cc: Beth Krell <beth@gpupartner.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-10T16:30:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Proposal: Hybrid Reserved Pool + GPU Indexation for NimbusAI

Tom —

Attached is v3 of the proposal (nimbus-proposal-v3.pdf) and the sensitivity workbook (gpu-price-index-template.xlsx). Executive highlights:
- Proposed term: 18 months (start May 1) with 6-month auto-extension option.
- Committed capacity tiers: Conservatively sized (0.9M token-hrs/mo), Target (1.2M token-hrs/mo), Peak (1.6M token-hrs/mo) with our recommended pick: Target (1.2M).
- SKU exchange: up to 20% per quarter across certified families; one-time provisioning rebalancing fee = $X per exchange.
- Indexation: 3-month rolling GPU index (GPUPartner) with +/-10% collar and annual true-up. Effective price floor 75% of current list, floor only applies if average utilization >= 60% of committed pool.
- Approval: Redwood can offer up to 15% commercial concession without VP approval; >15% requires VP Sales + EVP Finance sign-off. Finance has provisionally greenlit the structure.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm which tier (Conservative / Target / Peak) you want priced and whether you want the 6-month extension.
2) Beth — can you confirm the GPUPartner index methodology so we can pin the reference spreadsheet?
3) If Nimbus wants a different collar (e.g., 15%), flag that and we'll run sensitivity and route approvals.

I'll convert to a DocuSign after we land on tier and collar. Attaching links to HubSpot deal and draft DocuSign for internal tracking.

Aisha Rahman
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: nimbus-proposal-v3.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB), gpu-price-index-template.xlsx (spreadsheet)
